extension.description: Reviews mcp-guard runs that start processes, approve a trust baseline or write message bodies to disk. proxy, test-injection --run and --live (inspect, lock, ui, snapshot save) start the MCP servers named in a config or on the command line, or the given agent script. lock writes the lock file that later runs compare against, so running it approves the current tools, including a changed description. proxy --record-bodies keeps full JSON-RPC messages, which can contain secrets, in the journal. Static audits (inspect, scan, ui, snapshot save and diff without --live), journal export, test-injection without --run, and direct runs with --help or --version (except proxy, whose later arguments go to the server) are not matched by this extension; Guard's default handling for commands no rule matches still applies to them. Covers the mcp-guard and mcp-guard-audit executables (including .cmd/.exe). uvx, uv tool run and pipx run launches of the package are covered by command.package.python.
extension.name: mcp-guard command protection

permissions.description: Identifies mcp-guard runs that start an MCP server or an agent script: proxy, test-injection --run, and --live on inspect, lock, ui and snapshot save.
permissions.label: mcp-guard server launch
safer_guidance: Audit the config statically first: mcp-guard inspect CONFIG reads the file and starts nothing.
Check which command each server entry runs before allowing --live, proxy or test-injection --run.

permissions.description: Identifies mcp-guard lock, which writes the trusted baseline that later inspect --lock and proxy --lock runs compare against.
permissions.label: mcp-guard lock approval
safer_guidance: Compare first with mcp-guard inspect CONFIG --lock mcp-guard.lock: it lists what changed since the lock was written and writes nothing.
Approve a new lock only after a person has reviewed those changes.

permissions.description: Identifies mcp-guard proxy --record-bodies, which writes full JSON-RPC messages, including arguments and results that can contain secrets, to the journal file.
permissions.label: mcp-guard full-body journal
safer_guidance: Record without --record-bodies: the journal then keeps methods, ids, sizes and outcomes only.
Keep a full-body journal out of version control and delete it after use.

rules.description: Identifies mcp-guard proxy, test-injection --run, and inspect, lock, ui or snapshot save with --live. They start the MCP servers named in the config or given with --server (any command, or an http(s) URL that is contacted), or run the agent script given to test-injection. Covers the mcp-guard and mcp-guard-audit executables (including .cmd/.exe). uvx, uv tool run and pipx run launches of the package are covered by command.package.python.
safer_alternatives: Audit the config statically first: mcp-guard inspect CONFIG reads the file and starts nothing.
Check which command each server entry runs before allowing --live, proxy or test-injection --run.
rules.title: mcp-guard server launch

rules.description: Identifies mcp-guard lock. It writes (or with --update, migrates) the lock file that inspect --lock and proxy --lock treat as the approved state, so running it approves the current servers and tools, including a description or annotation that changed since the last lock. Covers the mcp-guard and mcp-guard-audit executables (including .cmd/.exe). uvx, uv tool run and pipx run launches of the package are covered by command.package.python.
safer_alternatives: Compare first with mcp-guard inspect CONFIG --lock mcp-guard.lock: it lists what changed since the lock was written and writes nothing.
Approve a new lock only after a person has reviewed those changes.
rules.title: mcp-guard lock approval

rules.description: Identifies mcp-guard proxy --record-bodies. The journal then keeps every JSON-RPC message in full, including tool arguments and results that can hold tokens or file contents. Without it, the journal keeps no bodies. Covers the mcp-guard and mcp-guard-audit executables (including .cmd/.exe). uvx, uv tool run and pipx run launches of the package are covered by command.package.python.
safer_alternatives: Record without --record-bodies: the journal then keeps methods, ids, sizes and outcomes only.
Keep a full-body journal out of version control and delete it after use.
rules.title: mcp-guard full-body journal

safer_alternatives: Run mcp-guard inspect CONFIG without --live: a static audit starts nothing.
Review inspect --lock output before writing a new lock.
